reason: The hypothesis makes multiple specific claims about surface energies, segregation, diffusion, and evaporation in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the specific behavior of this complex quinary nanoalloy under the stated conditions.
premises: Au and Cu have lower surface energies than Co, Ni, Pt in the alloy
Surface energy differences drive Au and Cu to segregate to nanoparticle surfaces
Segregation and reshaping (elliptical to spherical) enhance local atomic diffusion
The process is kinetically controlled, leading to evaporation of Au and Cu
High-entropy stabilization and sluggish diffusion are insufficient to prevent this in sub-10 nm particles above ~673 K
